oneTimers: Stock-based compensation and related employer payroll taxes totaled $89.507M in Q2 across cost of revenue and operating expenses — the main reason GAAP shows an operating loss while non-GAAP operating income was $56.953M.
Amortization of acquired intangible assets was $1.982M in Q2 — also excluded from non-GAAP results.
Acquisition-related and other expenses were $0.162M in Q2 — excluded from non-GAAP results.
No one-time compensation charge landed in Q2 2024: the $15.000M one-time compensation charge in the six-month figures dates to the first quarter of 2024.
A year ago, Q2 2023's net loss included a $50.300M loss on extinguishing convertible debt — most of the year-over-year improvement in the net loss is that charge not repeating.
otherDetail: Interest income of $21.715M, less $1.218M of interest expense, plus other income, net of $0.269M — total non-operating income of $20.766M.

takeaways.text: Revenue hit $401.0M, up 30% YoY from $308.5M a year ago, and annualized revenue crossed $1.6 billion. Large customers — those paying over $100,000 a year — rose to 3,046 from 2,352, and paying customers overall grew 21% to 210,166. Remaining performance obligations — work customers have already committed to — stood at $1,421.0M, with 69% expected within 12 months.
takeaways.title: Growth held at 30% and crossed $1.6B annualized

takeaways.text: GAAP loss from operations narrowed to $34.7M, or 8.7% of revenue, versus a $56.2M loss a year ago, as operating expenses grew 20% — slower than revenue. $20.8M of non-operating income, mostly $21.7M of interest income, narrowed the net loss to $15.1M versus $94.5M a year ago. Excluding $89.5M of stock-based compensation and other items, non-GAAP operating income was $57.0M, a 14.2% margin. Operating cash flow was $74.8M, 19% of revenue.
takeaways.title: A narrower operating loss, still GAAP-unprofitable

takeaways.text: Dollar-based net retention was 112%, meaning existing paying customers spent 12% more than they did a year earlier — down from 115% a year ago. Paying customers overall grew 21% to 210,166, and large customers — those paying over $100,000 a year — rose to 3,046 from 2,352.
takeaways.title: Existing customers keep spending more

verdict: Cloudflare grew revenue 30% to $401.0M and crossed $1.6 billion in annualized revenue, but $89.5M of stock-based compensation kept it GAAP-unprofitable with a $15.1M net loss, even as operating cash flow hit $74.8M.
